page: The Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-1200s-amd is a memory-oriented server within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, delivering 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the processor provides 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 192 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio designed for memory-intensive processing. High-speed local persistence is supplied through a bundled 1200 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one public IPv4 address. The server contains no GPU acceleration hardware.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong parallel processing capabilities, placing stress-ng multi-core (67,555.75) and Geekbench multi-core (16,500.0) in the top quartile of tested instances. Additional top-tier results include Geekbench image processing at 14,845.0, text processing at 2,491.0, and PassMark physics at 7,022.49. In contrast, single-thread compute metrics align with the middle 50% tier, showing a Geekbench single-core score of 1,896.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also position within average bands, registering 141.36 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 71.93 GB/sec for writes. Operational tests show 42.05 million Redis SET operations per second and 21.64 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

Architecturally, the platform supports AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2 instruction extensions, though it lacks AVX-512 support. This constraint affects vectorized compute efficiency in specialized scientific workloads, reflected in medium 7B model LLM inference rates of 17.66 text generation tokens per second. The large RAM density and fast NVMe storage offer qualitative cost advantages for memory-resident architectures. Best-fit use cases include in-memory key-value databases, relational database servers, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency web application backends.

It features an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation with no discrete GPU hardware. Hardware instruction sets include AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while omitting AVX-512 extensions. In synthetic testing, the instance exhibits top-quartile performance in multi-core metrics, scoring 67,555.75 in stress-ng and 16,500.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Single-core throughput, along with uncached memory reads (141.36 GB/sec) and writes (71.93 GB/sec), rank within average tiers.
